REP: Tom, thanks for having me back. Last time you mentioned the district was looking at clinical services for next year, so I'd like to understand where that stands before I say anything about RapidPanel. Sound okay?
CUSTOMER: Sure. Good timing, actually. We just got our goals for next year.
REP: What's on that list?
CUSTOMER: Two big things. Clinical service revenue, because dispensing margins keep shrinking, and patient visits per week. Corporate wants every store to offer at least one service beyond vaccines by next fall. They're tying part of the managers' bonus to it, so everybody's paying attention.
REP: What clinical services are you running today besides vaccines?
CUSTOMER: Vaccines and some medication reviews for the Medicare plans. We tried cholesterol screening at two stores a few years ago, but it fizzled.
REP: What made it fizzle?
CUSTOMER: Nobody owned it. The machine sat in a closet, the staff forgot how to run it, and when the techs who were trained left, that was the end of it. Nobody was measured on it, so nobody fought for it.
REP: That's useful to know. If you added testing, how would the district decide whether it was working after the first season?
CUSTOMER: Tests per store per week, mostly, and whether it brings in new patients. If a store is doing fewer than five tests a week by February, it's not worth the training time. My district manager is very numbers-driven. If she can't see it on a weekly report, it didn't happen.
REP: Got it. RapidPanel runs strep, flu and COVID tests on one reader, and the reader keeps a log of every test, so you'd get tests per store per week without anyone keeping a spreadsheet.
CUSTOMER: The tracking would help. But corporate legal is nervous about liability. If a pharmacist misses a strep case and a kid ends up in the hospital, that's on us.
REP: The tests are CLIA-waived, and the protocol we provide has a clear rule: any patient with a negative result who still has symptoms gets referred to a provider the same day, and the documentation template records that the referral was made. Most chains add it to their existing clinical services policy.
CUSTOMER: Okay. I'd have to send that to legal, but it's a start. If another chain already uses that protocol, that would carry a lot of weight with them.
REP: Who else besides legal weighs in on a decision like this?
CUSTOMER: My district manager, Carla Simmons. She signs off on anything that needs training hours. And purchasing will push back, because we already have a deal with our wholesaler's house-brand strep test.
REP: Good to know. What do you like about the house brand, and what's missing?
CUSTOMER: It's cheap. That's the main thing. But it's a visual read, no reader, so every pharmacist reads the line a little differently, and there's no record unless someone writes it down. It doesn't do flu, either. So during flu season we'd still be sending people out the door, which kind of defeats the point.
REP: Cheap matters, especially across six stores, so I get why purchasing likes it. Where RapidPanel earns its price is exactly what you just described. The reader takes the judgment call out of reading the line, every result is logged with a timestamp, and the same reader runs flu and COVID, so you're not training staff on three different products. The kits run about two dollars more than a typical house-brand strep test, and you'd make that back in documentation time alone. Does that make the price difference easier to defend?
CUSTOMER: Yeah. Documentation is a sore point for Carla. She'd care about that. We got dinged on a state inspection last year for incomplete vaccine records, and she still brings it up at every district meeting.
REP: Then here's what I'd suggest. Let's pilot it here first. I'll put together a one-page pilot plan with the protocol for legal, and I'll book thirty minutes with you and Carla. Is Wednesday the 7th at nine open for both of you?
CUSTOMER: Carla's here Wednesday mornings for the district call, so nine works.
REP: Great. I'll send the pilot plan and the protocol to you both by Friday, so legal can look at it before we meet on Wednesday the 7th at nine.
CUSTOMER: Perfect. Thanks, Maya.
